proposals.evidence: DEDR1834 gives Tamil kuḷir cool with past -nt-, kuḷirmai/kuḷumai coolness and Malayalam kuḷirma/kuḷir cold. Survey gɨḷime/galima/galindatɨ/gelica and Mannan kuḍiru are comparative cold-family variants preserving source initial voicing, nominal or participial endings and lateral/retroflex notation. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

proposals.evidence: DEDR404 gives Tamil āṟu with past āṟi- cool/grow cold, Malayalam āṟuka and Kannada āṟu grow cool. These āriya/ārin-/āriyad-/ārud-/āriyott- cold responses retain that cooling verb with ordinary participial/adjective endings and exact source spellings. Longer serial constructions remain unanalysed. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

proposals.evidence: DEDR601 gives Tamil uṇaṅku, Malayalam uṇaṅṅuka, Kannada oṇagu, Tulu oṇuṅgelu/uṇuṅgu/nuṅgu dry and dry up. These unag-/oṇag-/voṇag-/nuṅg- survey responses preserve that drying stem, ordinary adjectival endings and initial glide; potentially competing nānt-/nan- readings are excluded. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.
